description: Explicit enforcement surface for every scripts/qa gate. Verified by scripts/qa/test-qa-gate-surface.sh, which runs in the ci.yml governance job. A script on disk that is absent here fails the gate, and so does an entry whose script no longer exists.

enforcementKinds.ci-required: Executed by a GitHub Actions workflow on every push/PR. Requires workflow, job, and providerIsolation. Must never be able to reach a real provider binary.
enforcementKinds.manual-runbook: Executed by a human following the owner QA document. Requires reason and owner.
enforcementKinds.scheduled: Executed by a scheduled workflow, not on push/PR. Requires reason and owner in addition to workflow and job.

providerIsolationModes.no-provider: The script never applies a manifest bundle that declares an unpinned claude/codex agent driver.
providerIsolationModes.fixture-pinned: Every claude/codex agent in the named fixture bundle also declares binary: fake-*.
providerIsolationModes.path-shadow: The script copies a fake provider into an isolated bin directory and prepends it to PATH before starting a daemon.

supportFileRoles.fixture: Input data or a fake executable consumed by a gate. Never invoked as a gate itself, so it has no enforcement of its own.
supportFileRoles.library: Shared shell or ruby sourced by one or more gates. Runs only inside its callers, so it inherits their enforcement.

commandSources.description: What each CI job puts on PATH, so a ci-required gate's `command -v` preamble can be checked against the job that runs it. FR-134 found three ci-required gates exiting on `missing command: rg` before their first assertion, in two jobs that had been green-lit by a wiring check which only asked whether they were referenced.
commandSources.runnerBaselineReason: Present on both ubuntu-latest and macos-latest runner images. This is the one input that cannot be derived from the repository, so it is declared — and deliberately minimal: anything a job could plausibly need to install is left out, which makes the check strict rather than permissive. ripgrep is absent from both images and is exactly what this list must not paper over.

workspaceScope.reason: No job in .github/workflows installs the Tauri and webkit system dependencies, so orchestrator-gui has never been built on Linux. The sibling test and clippy jobs exclude it; a ci-required gate that runs the workspace without that exclusion is not duplicating them, it is a superset whose extra part cannot pass. DD-139 recorded this as an accepted duplication cost, which was wrong. Building the GUI on Linux belongs to FR-076 requirement 1.

providerStubs.description: Installs claude and codex stubs that exit 97. Required in every job that runs a ci-required gate whose provider isolation is anything other than no-provider, so that isolation is never the single barrier. FR-127 installed them inline in the governance job only, which left the coordination-strangler job — whose gate rests entirely on fixture pinning — with no second line at all.

exemptJobs.reason: every ci-required gate in this job is no-provider: neither test-slack-live-certification.sh nor certify-slack-managed-live.sh applies a manifest bundle, and the recorded-contract fixtures contain no agent driver at all

Offline: reads git ls-files and the shell files' own text. Forbids, in any tracked *.sh that enables pipefail, a pipeline stage after the first whose command is grep/rg with -q, --quiet, --silent or -m. The reader leaves on the first match, the producer dies of EPIPE, and pipefail makes that the pipeline's answer - so a successful match reports as a failed one, or, where the match feeds the failing branch, a violation reports as clean (FR-145). Scope is a property read from each file rather than from this manifest, deliberately: the hazard has nothing to do with whether a script is ci-required, and qa-doc-lint.sh and coverage-governance.sh are run by ci.yml while absent from here.

scripts.note: Run with FR126_FAST=1 in CI. The repository-wide gates that the default mode re-runs (fmt, clippy, workspace tests, coordination strangler, coverage fixtures, qa-doc-lint) all execute as sibling jobs in the same workflow, so the certifying aggregate is the workflow, not this single invocation.
scripts.workspaceScopeReason: The unexcluded `cargo test --workspace` sits behind `FR126_FAST != 1`, and ci.yml runs this gate with FR126_FAST=1, so CI never reaches it. It runs in the local release aggregate on macOS, where the Tauri frameworks are system libraries — and that is currently the only place orchestrator-gui is compiled at all, since the sibling test and clippy jobs exclude it and no job installs its dependencies. Excluding it here to match them would delete the crate's last coverage rather than align anything. FR-076 requirement 1 owns building it in CI.
